title: Ecuador says it has complained to FIFA over Mexican fans’ pre-World Cup game antics
content:
The Ecuadorian Football Federation (FEF) has filed a complaint with FIFA for what it called “off-field incidents” ahead of Ecuador’s World Cup round-of-32 match versus Mexico.

Ecuador’s complaint comes after videos emerged online on Tuesday purportedly showing Mexico fans staging an impromptu fan fest outside their rival’s team hotel, the night before their knockout round game at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

The videos showed Mexico fans playing music, dancing, chanting, revving vehicle engines, honking horns and setting off fireworks. This type of gamesmanship is seen often throughout Latin America club and international football ahead of high-stakes matches, as well as in the English Premier League and mainland Europe.

The FEF, however, referred to such behavior as “conduct (that) falls far short of the principles of fair play, equity, and unity that a football World Cup should represent.”

“We trust that these unsportsmanlike acts will not overshadow the football celebration that unites two brotherly nations, and that respect, healthy competition, and fair play — the values that give meaning to a World Cup — will prevail at all times,” the FEF statemnt continued.

The statement continued with FEF asking “relevant authorities” to curb similar incidents and to “adopt the necessary measures to safeguard the safety of our players, coaching staff, and fans.” Ecuador arrived in Mexico City yesterday.

Ecuador head coach Sebastian Beccacece told reporters on Monday that what was supposed to be a six-hour flight from Columbus, Ohio, where the team has been based during the World Cup, turned into a nine-hour trip. “We don’t know why that happened,” Beccacece said. “I apologize for our tired faces. But we’ll deal with it. No matter where we play, we’ll compete. We won’t complain. We don’t have any excuses.”

The Mexican Football Federation declined to comment. FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
